Drag-and-drop uploads no longer crash Chromium-based browsers, and the app now warns when it is opened over an insecure (plain-HTTP) connection.

## Fixed

- **Drag-and-drop no longer crashes Chrome/Edge.** On some Chromium and Edge setups, dropping a file onto the upload area crashed the browser tab with `RESULT_CODE_KILLED_BAD_MESSAGE`. The trigger was the `webkitGetAsEntry()` directory walk that Chromium runs for drag-and-drop (the file picker and Firefox never use it, which is why both kept working). featherdrop only takes a single file, so it now reads the dropped file straight from the drop event and skips that path entirely.

## Added

- **Insecure-context notice.** When featherdrop is opened over plain HTTP (for example by IP), it now shows a banner that some features are limited there (large uploads fall back to memory, streamed downloads are off). Over HTTPS the full pipeline is enabled.
